html:
The Ahantchuyuk were one of the bands of the Kalapuya people, living along the Pudding River in the northern Willamette Valley of present-day Oregon. They spoke a dialect of Central Kalapuya.

Like other Kalapuya, they lived from camas bulbs, acorns, berries, deer and fish, and burned the valley grasslands each year to keep them open. Their neighbours included the Atfalati to the north and the Santiam to the south.

Malaria and other diseases in the 1830s killed most Kalapuya. French Canadian settlers then farmed their land, known as French Prairie. In 1855 the survivors signed a treaty and were moved to the reservation of the Confederated Tribes of Grand Ronde.
sum: The Ahantchuyuk were one of the bands of the Kalapuya people, living along the Pudding River in the northern Willamette Valley of present-day Oregon. They spoke a dialect of Central Kalapuya.
